..
Issued at 345 AM CDT Thu Sep 3 2026

The main weather story continues to be the week long heat wave
that we are experiencing through Saturday. We continued the
Extreme Heat Warning across the CWA through 7 pm Friday for 
heat indices peaking around 105 or higher. Extended the Extreme
Heat Warning until 7 pm Saturday for sw 1/3rd of CWA from 
Rushville to Springfield to Robinson sw for heat indices still 
approaching 105F Sat afternoon. The remainder of CWA may need 
also need a heat headline on Saturday especially if backdoor 
cold front moves in slower since we currently are forecast heat 
indices 100-105F over central/ne CWA. The NWS HeatRisk is in the
Extreme Category (level 4 of 4) for much of CWA today and
Friday, and Major Category (level 3 of 4) from I-74 sw on 
Saturday with Extreme Category just sw of CWA. Cooling Centers
over IL are listed at... keepcool.illinois.gov 
Today and Fridays temperatures and humidity levels similar to  
yesterday with highs in the mid 90s to near 100F (warmest sw 
CWA) with dewpoints in upper 60s to mid 70s (highest n/ne CWA)
and afternoon heat indices 100-110F. SW winds actually a bit 
lighter today and Friday than past few days so lighter winds 
providing less relief from the heat. Highs Saturday slightly
cooler ne CWA in lower 90s, while mid to upper 90s over sw half
of CWA and upper 90s in southeast IL. Heat indices still
reaching 100-105F Sat afternoon and possibly higher from
Springfield to Robinson south/sw. 

Springfield reached 100F yesterday and just one degree from the
record high. The last time Springfield got that hot was July 31,
2012. Lawrenceville airport has reached 101 past two days. Both
Springfield and Lawrenceville to make a run for the century run
again today and Friday. 

A strong 593-595 decameter subtropical 500 mb high from the mid
MS river valley into the Carolinas will stay near IL (se of IL)
through Friday and continue the very hot and humid airmass over
the area. The best chance of convection today through Fri
evening will be north/ne of CWA closer to a frontal boundary
near the southern Great Lakes and upper Ohio river valley, and 
disturbances moving se from ND/MN across the Great Lakes region 
and ne Ohio river valley. We have less than 20% chance of
convection from mid afternoon until sunset from I-74 ne today.
MUCAPEs rise to 2000-3000 j/kg over ne CWA while 0-6km Bulk
Shear values rise to 20-30 kts by late afternoon from I-72
north. Bulk wind shear is weaker around 20 kts on Fri afternoon
though more unstable with MUCAPES 2500-3500 j/kg and highest in
ne CWA. Our pops are still below 20% on Friday but still could
see very isolated convection appear from mid Fri afternoon until
sunset over ne CWA. Then 20-30% chance of thunderstorms
overnight Fri night into Sat with highest pop ne CWA as backdoor
cold front moves into central IL during Saturday. SPC day1
outlook has marginal risk of severe from from Canton to
Champaign and Danville north from mid afternoon until sunset for
mainly gusty winds though hail may also occur. SPC Day2 outlook
has marginal risk of severe for mainly wind over all but far sw
CWA overnight Fri night. SPC Day3 Outlook has marginal risk of
severe storms over eastern CWA generally from highway 51 east on
Saturday afternoon for gusty winds and hail. WPC ERO keeps
marginal risk of excessive rainfall ne of CWA next few days
though can not rule out an isolated storm with very heavy rains
with PWATs 1.5-1.75 inches. 

The strong mid/upper level subtropical ridge retrogrades west
into the Great Plains early next week giving IL a break from the
impressive heat/humidity though still warmer than normal with
highs in the mid 80s ne CWA and upper 80s/lower 90s sw CWA. The
strong 500 mb ridge building back into IL Tue/Wed and likely 
bringing the high heat and humidity back to the area with highs 
in the 90s and afternoon heat indices approaching 100F (highest
on Wed).

The Climate Prediction Center (CPC) 8-14 Day Outlook for Sep
10-16th has 65-75% chance of above normal temperatures over
central and southeast IL with precipitation trending near
normal.
